title: Les autres chefs-d’oeuvres
medium: sculptures, which came to the museum separately, have been brought together as all three represent characters from the scene of the Deposition from the Cross. This is a very rare theme in 11th-century sculpture, presenting the moment when Christ is removed from the cross on which he was tortured. Today, the association of these objects has been reconsidered.

title: Les autres chefs-d’oeuvres
medium: ceramic does not bear any signature, it is difficult to say exactly where it comes from. But it is sometimes possible to make a comparison of style with other signed works. In the case of this plaque, a problem arises: it reminds us as much the faience of Lille as it does of that of Rouen. How do you decide between them?

title: Les autres chefs-d’oeuvres
medium: drawings to the Société des Sciences, de l’Agriculture et des Arts de Lille – the forerunner of the Palais des Beaux-Arts. The collection was over 1,300 strong, and mostly came from Italy. In addition, there was a "Wax Head from the Time of Raphael". But who is hiding behind this pretty face?

title: Les autres chefs-d’oeuvres
medium: sculpture of the Virgin and Child surprises us with its compact format. This is no faux pas on the part of the sculptor, but simply a material history punctuated by a variety of different types of damage...
